Set the digits of the numbers in the cells

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_digits.Rd

plan_digits() gives the decimals (or significant digits) the open tokens of the plan_cells() templates take — {mean}, {p:%}, as opposed to {mean:.2f}, which already says. It is the verb a study writes twice: a house rule for every table, then one variable's own. A later layer wins key by key, and a statistic the narrower entry says nothing about falls through to the wider one. On a plan of a finished table it formats the numbers themselves, with fmt_numeric().

Usage

plan_digits(.plan, ..., rounding = NULL)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

...

The digits, keyed as plan_cells()' templates are (an analysis variable, a stat group, a context, continuous / categorical, or one unnamed entry for every cell). Each value is:

one number

the decimals of every open token in that entry, plan_digits(1), plan_digits(AGE = 0).

a vector named by statistic

each statistic its own, continuous = c(mean = 1, sd = 2, median = 1).

"4s"

4 significant digits instead of decimals, as the token grammar's {mean:.4s}; it may be mixed in a named vector, c(mean = "4s", n = 0).

A key may also be a row key (a column of the long frame, such as PARAMCD), its digits given value by value: one of the values above for each, PARAMCD = c(ALT = 1, BILI = 3) or PARAMCD = list(ALT = c(mean = 1, sd = 2), BILI = 3) — a define's SignificantDigits one parameter at a time. The rows carrying that value take them after the analysis variable's own and before the context's, the kind's and the default; a value the rows do not carry is ignored, so one map can serve every table. On a finished table (a source that is already the table, or plan_cells(stats = "rows")) a key that names a column formats that column, and .rows formats the value columns by the text of the label column: plan_digits(.rows = c(N = 0, Mean = 1, SD = "3s")). A key that reaches neither a variable nor a column is an error.

A number of decimals is one whole number, 0 or more; a significant count is "<n>s" with n 1 or more ("0s" is an error). A vector of more than one value is named (by statistic, or by value for a row key). Anything else — 1.5, -1, Inf, NA, TRUE, "2" on its own, "x", c(1, 2) unnamed, a zero-length vector — stops at the verb, naming the key. (A whole number as text, "0", is read as decimals inside a named vector, as c(mean = "4s", n = 0) makes it.)

A later call replaces a key's entry as a whole: AGE = c(mean = 1, sd = 2) followed by AGE = c(mean = 0) leaves mean only for AGE, and its sd then takes the next wider key's digits.

rounding

The tie-breaking family for the run, as widen_ard(rounding = ) takes it. Last wins. A study sets the rule once with options(rtfreporter.rounding = ); give it here only for a table that departs from it.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 6),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "AGE", "WEIGHT", "WEIGHT", "SEX", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, NA, NA, NA, "F", "M"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c(rep("continuous", 4), rep("categorical", 2)), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "sd", "mean", "sd", "n", "n"), 2),
  stat      = c(61.24, 9.812, 72.456, 12.345, 12, 8,
                63.51, 10.218, 70.12, 11.874, 9, 11))
p <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean} ({sd})"),
             categorical = "{n}")

# Minimal: one decimal for every open token (the counts too)
p |> plan_digits(1) |> plan_apply("table")
#>    group     label     Placebo      Active
#> 1    AGE Mean (SD)  61.2 (9.8) 63.5 (10.2)
#> 2 WEIGHT Mean (SD) 72.5 (12.3) 70.1 (11.9)
#> 3    SEX         F        12.0         9.0
#> 4    SEX         M         8.0        11.0

# The house rule (SD one more than the mean, counts whole), then
# WEIGHT, measured more finely, one more again
p |>
  plan_digits(continuous = c(mean = 1, sd = 2), categorical = c(n = 0)) |>
  plan_digits(WEIGHT = c(mean = 2, sd = 3)) |>
  plan_apply("table")
#>    group     label        Placebo         Active
#> 1    AGE Mean (SD)    61.2 (9.81)   63.5 (10.22)
#> 2 WEIGHT Mean (SD) 72.46 (12.345) 70.12 (11.874)
#> 3    SEX         F             12              9
#> 4    SEX         M              8             11

# A lab table: the digits by parameter, as a define gives them
lb <- data.frame(
  ARM = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 4),
  PARAMCD = rep(rep(c("ALT", "BILI"), each = 2), 2),
  variable = "AVAL", .label = NA, .kind = "continuous",
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "sd"), 4),
  stat = c(31.234, 4.102, 0.612, 0.1234, 33.111, 5.303, 0.707, 0.1515))
table_plan(lb, cols = "ARM", rows = c(param = "PARAMCD")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean} ({sd})")) |>
  plan_digits(PARAMCD = list(ALT = c(mean = 1, sd = 2), BILI = c(mean = 3, sd = 4))) |>
  plan_apply("table")
#>   param     label        Placebo         Active
#> 1   ALT Mean (SD)    31.2 (4.10)    33.1 (5.30)
#> 2  BILI Mean (SD) 0.612 (0.1234) 0.707 (0.1515)
